name: DSUM
description: DSUM adds the numeric values in a specified field (column) of the records in a database that match the given criteria.
tldr: Sums the values in a database column for rows that meet the criteria.

parameters.name: database
parameters.description: The range containing the database, including the header row as the first row.

parameters.name: field
parameters.description: The column to sum, given as the column label in quotes (e.g. "Yield") or its 1-based column index.

parameters.name: criteria
parameters.description: The range with a header row matching database column names and one or more condition rows; only matching records are summed.

basicExample.description: Sum the Yield of apple trees taller than 10
basicExample.explanation: The criteria A9:B10 (Tree=Apple, Height>10) matches two rows with Yield 14 and 10, which add up to 24.

advancedExamples.title: Field referenced by column index
advancedExamples.scenario: Sum Profit instead of Yield without editing the criteria
advancedExamples.description: Pass the 1-based column position of Profit (column 5) as the field argument.
advancedExamples.explanation: The same two matching rows have Profit 105 and 75, so the sum is 180.

advancedExamples.title: Combine with other conditions
advancedExamples.scenario: Sum Yield for apple trees with Age greater than 12
advancedExamples.description: Extend the criteria range with an Age column and condition >12 below the Apple/Height condition.
advancedExamples.explanation: Both tall apples (Age 20 and 15) exceed 12, so Yield 14 and 10 still sum to 24.

howItWorks: DSUM filters the database down to the rows matching the criteria range, then totals the numeric values found in the specified field column of those rows. Non-numeric and blank cells in the field are ignored by the sum.

howToSteps.name: Set up the database
howToSteps.text: Enter your table with a header row; here A1:E7 with Tree, Height, Age, Yield, Profit.

howToSteps.name: Set up criteria
howToSteps.text: Place criteria headers and values in a separate range, e.g. A9:B10.

limitations: Only numeric values in the field are summed; text and blanks are skipped.
Criteria header labels must exactly match database headers.
DSUM ignores records the criteria filter out entirely, so an over-broad criteria returns a larger total.

commonErrors.cause: The field was supplied as an unquoted column name rather than text or a number.
commonErrors.fix: Wrap the field name in quotes, e.g. "Yield", or use the column index.

commonErrors.cause: Criteria headers do not match the database, so no rows match.
commonErrors.fix: Make criteria header text identical to the database column name.

googleSheetsEquivalent.description: DSUM works identically in Google Sheets with the same arguments and criteria behavior.

faq.question: Can DSUM use a column index instead of a name?
faq.answer: Yes. Supply the 1-based column position, e.g. 4 for the fourth column, instead of "Yield".

faq.question: Does DSUM ignore text in the field?
faq.answer: Yes. Only numeric values in the matching rows are added; text and blank cells are ignored.

faq.question: How is DSUM different from SUMIF?
faq.answer: DSUM filters a multi-column database by an entire criteria range (with AND/OR logic), while SUMIF handles a single condition over one range.
